label: NOTIFICATIONS, TOASTS AND REWARD POPUPS, across genres — the toast stack and its lifetime, the banner, the coloured system line in chat, the actionable request card, the claim popup, the streak counter that outruns its own calendar, and what a shipped game does when one event has two different audiences
provenance: Fetched over the network on 2026-09-20 and read as text. Three kinds of source: (1) Roblox's own documentation, read from the raw creator-docs repository on raw.githubusercontent.com and from the engine reference YAML, because those are plain HTTP and are the canonical statement of what the engine already decides for you; (2) the community wikis of four shipped Roblox experiences — Roblox BedWars, Blox Fruits, Tower Defense Simulator and Adopt Me! — read as wikitext through each wiki's api.php endpoint, because Fandom serves its article HTML behind Cloudflare while api.php is open; (3) three DevForum resource threads, read as JSON through devforum.roblox.com/t/<id>.json, which is plain HTTP — that endpoint returns only the FIRST PAGE of a thread, about twenty posts, so a longer thread has to be paged through and the row says where it stopped. No image, no Luau source and no asset is copied here. Each row records the URL, how it was fetched and the date, so the claim can be re-checked. This file exists because the library already covered the DAILY REWARDS PANEL (screen-rewards.json) and had nothing at all on the channel that announces things — the toast, the banner, the coloured chat line, the request card — which is the surface every other screen hands its outcomes to.

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/reference/engine/classes/StarterGui.yaml — fetched with curl on 2026-09-20; the engine reference for StarterGui:SetCore(), whose SendNotification section is Roblox's own built-in notification primitive.
demonstrates: THE ENGINE HAS ALREADY CHOSEN THE CORNER. The documentation states the notification appears at the BOTTOM RIGHT of the screen. A game that draws its own toast top-right is not matching the platform, it is competing with it, and both will be on screen at once if anything ever calls SetCore.
TWO BUTTONS IS THE CEILING, stated outright: the notification may have up to two buttons. A three-choice notification is not a notification in this system; it is a dialog and belongs somewhere else.

Duration is a NUMBER OF SECONDS with a documented default of 5. That is the only hard lifetime figure found anywhere in this file, and it is the platform's, so a custom toast that lives noticeably longer or shorter than five seconds is making a choice against a known baseline rather than in a vacuum.

THE CALLBACK IS HANDED THE BUTTON'S TEXT, NOT AN INDEX OR AN ID. The BindableFunction 'should be invoked with the text of the button pressed'. That is a real trap: renaming a button label silently changes what the handler receives, so the label and the branch are coupled by string.

Title and Text are both REQUIRED; Icon, Duration, Callback, Button1 and Button2 are all optional. The minimum honest notification is therefore two lines of text, and everything else — including the icon — is decoration the platform does not insist on.

There is no field for priority, for a stack group, for a category, or for dismissal. The platform primitive has no concept of several notifications competing, which is why every kit below invents one.

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/includes/experience-notifications/implementation-create-notification-string.md plus .../guidelines.md, .../delivery-system.md and .../intro.md — all four fetched with curl on 2026-09-20; Roblox's documentation for out-of-experience notifications, i.e. the message that reaches a player who is not in the game.
demonstrates: THE TITLE IS NOT THE DEVELOPER'S TO WRITE. Notifications 'automatically use the title of your game as the notification title'. Everything the developer controls is body text, which means the body must never re-state the game's name — and the {experienceName} token exists precisely because you sometimes want it INSIDE the sentence instead.

The body is capped at 99 CHARACTERS and may carry unlimited custom parameters. A notification is therefore a TEMPLATE with holes — the documented examples fill in a quest count, an egg name, a race count and a friend's userId — not a string a script concatenates.

'There is no default game notification string, so this step is required.' The message must be authored on the Creator Dashboard and referenced by asset id. A notification's text is content with an id, versioned and moderated, not a literal in code.

THE THROTTLE IS ONE PER USER PER DAY, per experience, plus an aggregate daily cap across all experiences. That single slot is the whole design constraint: it forces a game to decide which one thing is worth a day, and it is why a generic 'come back and play' is not merely weak but actively spends the only slot there is.

DELIVERY IS NOT GUARANTEED, and the documentation LISTS SEVEN non-delivery cases: experience eligibility requirements not met, the recipient not opted in, the recipient's per-experience throttle reached, the recipient's aggregate daily throttle reached, missing or invalid request parameters, the notification string having been moderated, and — for notifications with user mentions — either the two players not being friends or the mentioned player having turned off 'Update friends about my activity?'. The last bullet splits in two, so it is eight outcomes on seven lines. They are not all silent: the same page says 'you receive transparent feedback when a user's throttle limit is reached.' Code that assumes a notification arrived is wrong on every path that does not report itself.

FALSE TIME PRESSURE IS BANNED BY NAME, and the example given is a notification telling a user to purchase within ten minutes or miss out. So is telling a user they will get something free when they will not, and disguising an advert as organic content. The countdown-and-scarcity vocabulary that reward popups reach for first is explicitly out of bounds on this channel.
'Games should not require users to turn on notifications in order to participate or advance in gameplay.' The notification channel may never be load-bearing for progression.

references.source: https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/wiki/Notification — read on 2026-09-20 through https://robloxbedwars.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Notification&prop=wikitext&format=json, because Fandom serves its article HTML behind Cloudflare while api.php is open. The page is a catalogue of every notification a shipped Roblox shooter sends and what causes each one.
demonstrates: ONE EVENT, TWO TEXTS, CHOSEN BY AUDIENCE. When a bed is destroyed, the losing team is told their own bed is gone and that they will no longer respawn; every OTHER team is told which team colour lost its bed. Same event, two strings, and the second one names a team the first does not have to. Audience is a property of the notification, not of the recipient's filter.

EVERY NOTIFICATION IS MANUALLY DISMISSIBLE. The page says all of them can be made to disappear by clicking on PC or tapping on mobile. A timed lifetime and a tap-to-dismiss are both present; neither replaces the other.

THE PAGE'S OWN COUNT IS STALE AND THE LIST IS THE USEFUL PART. It reads 'There are currently ten types of notifications:' and then names TWELVE — beds, teleportation, team upgrades, party, the Vulcan kit, bed alarms, custom-match commands, lucky blocks, a Tesla coil trap, spirits, friends and sudden death. The discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved, because nothing on the page says which two were added after the sentence was written. What matters is the AXIS: the types are named after the SUBSYSTEM that raises them, not after severity or tone. There is no 'info / warning / error' taxonomy anywhere on the page.

A MESSAGE THAT DID NOT COME FROM YOUR OWN ACTION CARRIES A BRACKETED SOURCE PREFIX. The bed-alarm message and the host-announcement message both open with the subsystem name in square brackets. The prefix is how the player knows the line was not caused by the button they just pressed.

REFUSALS RIDE THE SAME CHANNEL AS CELEBRATIONS. Not enough diamonds to repair a table, a party already at maximum size, a queue that could not be joined, an invalid item, a kit name that does not exist — all of these are notifications, in the same stack that announces a teammate's purchase. The toast channel is the error channel.

AN ACTIONABLE SOCIAL NOTIFICATION IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE ENTIRELY. The party invite is the only notification on the page given as a TABLE rather than as a quoted line: a caption reading PARTY INVITE, an image cell, and the sender's display name. A notification that wants an answer stops being a sentence and becomes a titled card with a picture slot in it. WHAT THAT PICTURE SLOT RENDERS IS NOT RECORDED HERE — the wikitext holds a placeholder image file, and no image was looked at for this file.

A COUNTDOWN IS EXPRESSED AS DISCRETE NOTIFICATIONS AT DECREASING INTERVALS, not as a persistent timer. Sudden death announces at 59 seconds, again at 10 seconds, then announces the event itself. Three fires, no widget.

WHEN A CAP IS HIT, THE MESSAGE NAMES WHAT WAS DESTROYED TO MAKE ROOM. Placing a second trap reports that the oldest trap has been destroyed; placing a ninth spirit reports that an older one has been removed. The game does not merely refuse — it says which thing it evicted.
A NOTIFICATION CLASS CAN BE SWITCHED OFF INDEPENDENTLY: friend-join notifications have their own settings toggle. Opt-out granularity is per class, not one global mute.

references.source: https://blox-fruits.fandom.com/wiki/System_Messages — read on 2026-09-20 through https://blox-fruits.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=System%20Messages&prop=wikitext&format=json, for the Cloudflare reason above. The page transcribes 174 in-game messages together with the event that causes each, in four tables: Boss (21 rows), Event (38), Player (81) and Island Secrets (34).
demonstrates: THE CHANNEL IS THE CHAT BOX, NOT A FLOATING TOAST. The page describes boss and event announcements as appearing in the chat boxes. A server-wide announcement rides the chat the player is already reading, which is why it survives a busy screen and why it leaves a scrollback.

COLOUR IS APPLIED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS ON ONE PAGE, AND THE SPLIT IS BY AUDIENCE. Three of the four tables declare one colour for the whole section — 'All of the following messages appear red in the chat boxes' heads Boss, Event and Island Secrets — so a server-wide announcement is red because of the CHANNEL it arrives on, not because of what it says. Per-message colour exists only in the Player Messages table, where the player's own outcomes carry red, a bright green, a gold-yellow, magenta, a blue-violet and one plain yellow. The vocabulary there is a tendency rather than a mapping: gold carries items found AND 'The event shop has been restocked!' AND 'NEW SKILL AVAILABLE!', and magenta carries materials AND 'Stored <Sword>'. What the page supports is that colour separates kinds of message inside one channel — not that each colour means exactly one thing.

AN OUTLINE ACCOMPANIES MOST COLOURED MESSAGES, NOT ALL OF THEM. Of the 37 lines the wiki renders with its colour template, 24 also carry the text-outline template and 13 do not — 'Item drop: <Item>', 'NEW SKILL AVAILABLE!', 'FIGHT!', 'Enemy is immune to physical attacks!', 'Super Dash ready!' and the two bounty-penalty lines among them. Roughly two thirds: enough to call the stroke the default treatment for coloured chat text, not enough to call it universal. The reason to want it is a design argument rather than a citation — coloured text over a chat window sitting on top of arbitrary game world loses the legibility the colour was meant to add.

ONE NOTIFICATION CAN HOLD TWO COLOURS AND TWO MEANINGS. Finding a fruit is announced in green and immediately followed, in the same message, by a red warning that dying before eating it will lose it. The reward and its caveat are one line, coloured differently — not two notifications, and not a reward with the caveat dropped.

REWARDS ARE ANNOUNCED PER RESOURCE, ONE LINE EACH — money earned, experience earned (with the weapon it was credited to in parentheses), fragments earned, materials obtained with a quantity, an item drop with its own marker. There is no combined 'you earned 3 things' summary anywhere on the page.

THE SAME EVENT ESCALATES ITS COPY BY A NUMERIC BAND. A player joining with 5M–14.9M bounty triggers a warning-toned announcement; 15M–30M triggers a louder one declaring a god has arrived. One event, two strings, selected by a threshold — the notification's volume is a function of a stat.

AN ERROR MESSAGE CARRIES THE REMEDY AND THE HOTKEY. The message for hitting an immune enemy states the problem, names the ability that fixes it, and puts the key to press in square brackets at the end. A refusal that does not say what to do instead is a refusal the player has to leave the game to understand.

A NOTIFICATION IS USED AS A ROUTE. An unclaimed gift is announced as a line telling the player to check the shop — the message's job is not to deliver the thing but to point at the screen that holds it.

MANY ANNOUNCEMENTS DELIBERATELY DO NOT NAME THEIR SUBJECT. A boss spawning is announced in-fiction — tremors heard, a shiver down the spine, a barrier broken — and the wiki's Cause column exists precisely because players cannot tell from the message alone which boss it means. This is a shipped game choosing atmosphere over legibility on purpose, and the community building a decoder ring for it.

FAILURE BY EXPIRY IS ANNOUNCED TOO. When nobody kills the boss in time, the timeout gets its own message; when a timed puzzle's window closes, the closing gets its own message. An event that ends because nothing happened still fires.

references.source: https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/Playtime_Rewards — read on 2026-09-20 through https://tds.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Playtime%20Rewards&prop=wikitext&format=json. The value of this page is its Update History, which is a dated, versioned record of one shipped reward popup being repeatedly corrected between September 2025 and April 2026.
demonstrates: THE STRONGEST RECORDED DECISION IN THIS FILE. In v1.75.2, on the same day the feature shipped, 'Claim pop-ups now display the item given instead of the name of the chest.' The popup originally named the CONTAINER the reward came out of. It was changed to name the thing the player actually received. A reward popup that says which box opened has told the player nothing they wanted to know.

In v1.75.3, playtime rewards began displaying HOW MANY chests they give, and reward pools became visible at all. A tier that hands out more than one thing has to say how many before the popup opens, or the popup is the first time the player learns the size of what they were waiting for.

In v1.76.0 the pool disclosure MOVED FROM AN EXPLICIT CONTROL TO HOVER: previously the reward pool list appeared on clicking a magnifying-glass icon, afterwards on hovering the chest. The odds went from something you had to go and find to something you fall over. That direction is worth arguing about on touch devices, where there is no hover.

Also in v1.76.0: 'Chest icons are now bigger' and 'Rewards are now displayed with an animation.' The claim moment acquired motion in a patch, after the data was already correct — the animation was the last thing added, not the first.
In v1.89.0 the consumable crate icons were REPLACED WITH GIFTBOXES. The icon vocabulary was changed so a reward tier reads as a gift rather than as an inventory item the player might already own.

A RECORDED DEFECT WORTH DESIGNING AGAINST, stated in the page's own bug line for v1.83.0: after one ad is played, every following ad is impossible to play 'even if the game makes it look like they are claimable', and it only resolves on rejoin. A control that renders in its claimable state while the thing behind it is exhausted is the specific failure a reward surface is most prone to.
The ladder is time-gated at 5, 15, 30, 60, 90 and 120 minutes, and v1.76.0 pushed every step after the first further out. The spacing of a playtime ladder is a tuned number, not a constant.
A watch-an-ad offer appears RANDOMLY rather than always, grants three extra boxes, and resets after 24 hours. The opportunity itself is an event that has to be announced when it appears.

THE STREAK NUMBER AND THE CALENDAR INDEX ARE TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS. The reward table is 28 days long and repeats, but 'the streak does not go down to 1, it will instead increase to 29.' The displayed streak keeps counting forever while the grid it indexes wraps. A day tile that renders the streak count is rendering the wrong number on day 29.

The table repeats WITHOUT any reward scaling for higher streaks — so a player on day 200 receives exactly what a player on day 4 receives. The ladder's escalation is inside one cycle only, and the long-term streak is a status number rather than an economic one.

THE 28-DAY LADDER HAS A SHAPE, AND THE SHAPE IS NOT THE SAME ON EVERY TRACK. All three current tracks share a skeleton — a premium crate on days 7, 14 and 21, and a single higher-grade Deluxe crate on day 28 — but the fill between those beats differs: Track A runs 16 currency days to 8 ticket days, Track B 13 to 11, Track C 12 to 12. The weekly beat is the structure and the final day is the only tier that differs in kind rather than in amount; 'currency on most days, a ticket on a few' is true of one track out of the three.

TWO PLAYERS' CALENDARS ARE NOT THE SAME CALENDAR, which means the reward grid cannot be a shared static layout. The page's CURRENT section is itself three tracks of 28 days — A, B and C — and it does not say how a player's track is chosen. The superseded version, headed 'Before 10th of June 2026', states the selection outright: 30 days, three tracks 'randomly chosen', one centred on spin tickets, one balanced, one on consumables, and 'the track chosen by the game was permanent and was unable to be changed.' RANDOM AND PERMANENT BELONG TO THAT OLDER VERSION ONLY. What governs the three current tracks is simply not on the page.

That earlier version also gated the next claim on a 16-HOUR COOLDOWN after accepting, rather than on a calendar midnight: 'After a login reward was accepted, it took 16 hours for the next reward to appear.' A 'daily' reward whose gate is a rolling cooldown shorter than a day drifts the player's claim time earlier every day. The page states no window for the CURRENT version — only that the streak resets 'if they are not claimed in the amount of time required' — so no figure is recorded for it here.

references.source: https://adoptme.fandom.com/wiki/Trade_System — read on 2026-09-20 through https://adoptme.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=Trade%20System&prop=wikitext&format=json. Read for its treatment of ACTIONABLE notifications — requests that arrive unasked and need an answer — rather than for trading.
demonstrates: THE COUNTDOWN AND THE CONFIRM CONTROL ARE THE SAME ELEMENT. A counter in the corner of the trade window counts from 5, and 'when the countdown ends, it turns into a green accept button.' The timer does not sit beside the button; it BECOMES the button. Nothing can be confirmed while the number is still counting.

THAT COUNTDOWN RESETS ON EVERY CHANGE, and the page states the reason: it prevents a player accidentally accepting after items were added, removed or replaced. The reset is not a delay for its own sake — it is the mechanism that guarantees the thing you are agreeing to is the thing you looked at.

AN UNANSWERED REQUEST EXPIRES. The page records plainly that a trade request left unanswered for too long will expire. An actionable notification has a lifetime like any other; it does not wait forever for an answer.

THE WARNING POPUP IS ASYMMETRIC AND DOES NOT BLOCK. When the game judges a trade unfair, the player giving too much is warned that scamming is bannable while the OTHER party is warned they may be getting scammed — two different texts for one event — and if both proceed the system grants 15 MORE SECONDS to reconsider. The intervention buys deliberation time rather than refusing.

A BLOCKED NOTIFICATION TELLS THE SENDER WHY. If the recipient has trades off or set to friends-only they receive nothing, and 'the player sending the trade will be prompted accordingly.' The non-delivery is itself a notification, aimed at the other end.

THE RECIPIENT'S CONSENT SETTING HAS THREE VALUES, NOT TWO: for backpack viewing a player may choose always allow, always ask, or never allow, and the default is always ask. 'Always allow' is the interesting one — it does not silence the notification, it removes the interaction that would have raised one.

AN ACTION CONFIRMS ITSELF IN TWO PLACES AT ONCE. Suggesting an item be removed flashes a red mark over the item itself AND writes a line into the trade chat. In-place feedback and a logged line are complementary: one is seen if you are looking at the object, the other if you are not.

THE PER-INTERACTION LOG IS ITS OWN CHANNEL. Trade chat notifications were added so players could keep track of changes made within a trade, and an inline accept/decline sits on individual log lines. A scoped event log with actions inside it is a third thing, distinct from both the global toast stack and a modal.

A COUNT IS RENDERED AS A BADGE IN A CORNER: the number of players spectating a trade is shown in the bottom-right of the trading window, with their emoji reactions running down the side. This is the only true numeric count badge found in any source read for this file.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/notifications-system-free-roblox-notification-system-gui-toasts-chat-messages-banner/4849898 — read on 2026-09-20 as JSON through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/4849898.json, which devforum serves over plain HTTP. A published notification kit describing its own structure; the only source read here that names the stacking model explicitly.
demonstrates: THREE CHANNELS FOR THREE SCOPES, named as separate things: a TOAST that stacks in a corner and goes to one player; a full-screen BANNER, a large centred card, for a server restart or an event going live, sent to everyone; and a CHAT SYSTEM MESSAGE in a chosen colour. The choice between them is the audience and the weight, not the content.

SEVEN TEMPLATES, and the split is by CONTENT SHAPE: title only, title with subtitle, image with title, image with title and subtitle, banner, banner with subtitle, and alert. A notification's template is chosen by which of those four slots are filled.

THE FAILURE NOTIFICATION IS DELIBERATELY GIVEN LESS CHROME THAN THE SUCCESS ONE. The Alert template is described as red text at the BOTTOM of the screen with NO CARD BEHIND IT, for what could not be done — not enough money, a full inventory. A refusal gets no panel, no icon and a different edge of the screen from everything else. That is the opposite of the usual instinct to make errors louder, and it is the most arguable decision in this row.

THE STACKING MODEL IS A SET OF ATTRIBUTES ON THE TEMPLATE FRAME ITSELF: Duration, Stack direction, MAX ON SCREEN, STACK GROUP, Sound, Animation, and which edge it slides in from. 'Max on screen' and 'stack group' are the two that answer what happens when several fire at once — there is a cap, and notifications are partitioned into groups that stack independently of each other.

STACK DIRECTION INCLUDES AN AUTOMATIC MODE — down, up, left, right, or away from the NEAREST EDGE on its own. A stack that grows toward the middle of the screen from wherever it was placed does not need its direction re-authored when it is moved.

THE TEMPLATE IS THE STACK'S ANCHOR: 'where you move it in Studio is where its notifications appear.' Position is authored by dragging a frame, not passed as an argument, which is why duplicating a template yields a second independent stack rather than a restyled first one.

BEHAVIOUR TRAVELS WITH THE COPY. Because duration, animation, stack direction and sound are attributes on the frame, duplicating a template produces one that already behaves — the styling and the timing are not in separate places.
THE ANIMATION VOCABULARY IS THREE NAMED ENTRIES — slide, fade, pop — plus the edge to slide from. Three is the whole set on offer.

FOUR announcements ship with the pack itself, each with an INDIVIDUAL OFF SWITCH: a rotating announcement, a friend joining, players joining and leaving, and a purchase. The post draws that boundary itself — 'Nothing is hooked into Roblox events except the four announcements above, and each of those has an off switch' — and each one is a ModuleScript in a Triggers folder, where 'anything you drop in there appears here with a switch of its own'. The switch-per-class is an EXTENSION POINT rather than a fixed catalogue. (The other events this kit is often shown announcing — a code redeemed, a pet hatching, a free spin, a session gift — belong to four separate companion packs under 'Works great with', and ALL FOUR ARE PAID: Codes System $4.99, Easy Pet System $14.99, Roulette System $7.99, Time Rewards System $4.99. That list carries six packs in all; the two free ones, Datastore & Purchase System and Sound System & Music Player, are not the ones raising those four events. None of them are triggers this pack ships.) The per-class opt-out is the same one the BedWars row records from the player's side.
A rotating message can be delivered either as a chat line OR as a toast — the same content, routed to a different channel, is treated as a configuration rather than as a different feature.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/product-banner-notify-best-way-to-notify/2212832 — read on 2026-09-20 as JSON through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/2212832.json. THAT ENDPOINT RETURNS ONLY THE FIRST PAGE: posts 1–22 of a thread whose own metadata reports 98 posts and a highest post number of 104. The remaining pages were fetched separately the same day with ?page=2 through ?page=5, so what is recorded below is the whole thread rather than its first screen. A banner notification module whose author documents its own defects, argues with the thread about how to fix one, and then ships the fix.
demonstrates: A BANNER IS EXACTLY THREE ELEMENTS, stated by the author as its composition: a Header, a Description and an Icon. Not a title and a blob — the icon is structural, not optional decoration.

THE SECOND LINE IS DIMMED, NOT JUST SMALLER. The API table describes the header as the big text and the message as 'the small and translucent text'. Hierarchy in a notification is carried by transparency as well as by size.

DURATION IS A PER-CALL ARGUMENT, positioned between the icon and the optional config table. Two notifications from the same template can have different lifetimes, decided by the caller at the moment it fires.

THE MODULE EXPOSES A PUBLIC COUNT OF ACTIVE NOTIFICATIONS. That this needed to become API — and that the author had to fix it after a user hit an error calling it — says the caller is expected to make decisions based on how many are already on screen. A design with no cap pushes the concurrency problem back to every call site.

A RECORDED ENGINE TRAP, ARGUED OUT IN THE REPLIES AND THEN RESOLVED IN PUBLIC. The author's own listed defect is that long text shrinks instead of expanding the card. A replier proposed bucketing the width by message length (post 11); another said to just use AutomaticSize on X (post 12); and the AUTHOR ANSWERED, in his own words, 'the thing is this ui uses SizeConstraint and it will not scale whether i like it or not even the autosize is on by X' (post 20). He names a size constraint without naming an instance class, so that post records the EFFECT and not the mechanism. The fix then appears in the post's own update log — Update 2.0, 'Longer Notifications are now possible and the notification will resize!' — and at post 41 the author says how it was done: 'Actually it was done with Automatic Size, but I had to a lot of things such as Scale to Offset, Dividing Components into little Frames and so much more.' So automatic sizing was not beaten by the engine; it cost a restructure of the card to use. A read that stops at post 20 has the trap without the ending, and this row did until it was re-fetched.

TEXT THAT SHRINKS TO FIT IS THE WRONG DEFAULT FOR A NOTIFICATION. The whole exchange above exists because the card held its size and the text gave way; the author lists distortion and stretching as a con of his own product.

THE AUTHOR'S SECOND STATED CON IS 'NOT CLICKABLE'. A notification that cannot be dismissed or acted on is recorded as a shortcoming by the person who built it, which is the same finding the BedWars catalogue states from the other direction.

THERE IS NO BROADCAST. Asked how to send to everyone from the server, the author's answer is to loop over the player list and call once per player; omitting the player argument on the server returns an error rather than defaulting to all. 'To everyone' is a thing a notification API has to be given on purpose.

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/badge-free-customizable-badge-notification-system/4695996 — read on 2026-09-20 as JSON through https://devforum.roblox.com/t/4695996.json. An open-source module whose entire reason to exist is replacing Roblox's built-in badge-award notification.
demonstrates: THE REASON GIVEN FOR REPLACING THE PLATFORM NOTIFICATION IS STYLE, NOT FUNCTION: the author states Roblox's default badge notifications work well but offer little customisation, and that he wanted them to MATCH THE GAME'S UI. The most common motivation for a custom notification layer is that the built-in one belongs to a different design system.

The five things the author had to add to make that true, listed as the feature set: custom colours, custom title and description text, custom badge artwork, an optional sound, and control over presentation. Those five are the surface area of a notification's styling.

SOUND IS OPTIONAL AND PASSED AT AWARD TIME — the award call takes a GUI-properties table and a sound-properties table as separate arguments. Sound is treated as a per-award property, not a property of the notification type.
A BADGE CARRIES AN ACTIVE FLAG IN ITS OWN DEFINITION, alongside its name and id, so a badge can exist and be non-awardable without being deleted.

Badge ownership checking is part of the same module as the notification. Whether to show the award at all is a question about server state, and the thing that answers it ships with the thing that draws it.

The author's own 'current limitations' note says animations are handled by the module's built-in system and are not yet customisable — recorded here because it marks where a replacement notification layer typically stops short of the thing it replaced.

references.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/production/publishing/badges.md — fetched with curl on 2026-09-20; Roblox's own documentation for creating and awarding badges.
demonstrates: THE BADGE ICON IS CROPPED TO A CIRCLE BY THE UPLOAD PIPELINE. The template is 512×512 and 'the upload process trims and crops the badge image into a circular icon', so anything outside the circle is lost. A badge notification's art has to be composed for a circle before it is ever composed for the card it sits in.

AWARDING IS GATED ON A FLAG THE DASHBOARD OWNS: GetBadgeInfoAsync returns IsEnabled, and the documented safe pattern checks it before calling AwardBadgeAsync. A disabled badge can be awarded by code that does not check, and nothing on screen would say so.

BOTH THE INFO FETCH AND THE AWARD ARE WRAPPED IN pcall in Roblox's own example, with a warn on each failure path. The award that triggers a notification has two independent ways to fail before the notification is the question.
GetBadgeInfoAsync returns Name, IsEnabled, Description and IconImageId — the four fields a custom award notification needs, which means a badge toast never has to hardcode its own text or art.

Badge creation is rate-limited to five free per 24-hour GMT period, with each additional badge in that period costing 100 Robux. Order is AUTHORED rather than chronological: a new badge 'is placed at the end of the badge list' and the dashboard carries a drag-and-drop reordering page. ('You can reorder up to 50 badges at once using the drag-and-drop interface' is a per-operation batch limit; the doc states no cap on how many badges a game may hold.)

rules.rule: Pick the channel by AUDIENCE AND WEIGHT first, and only then design the thing: a toast for one player's own outcome, a banner for something happening to the whole server, a coloured chat line for an announcement that should leave a scrollback, a titled card carrying the sender's name for something that needs an answer.
rules.why: The notification kit names toast, banner and chat message as three separate mechanisms with three scopes, Blox Fruits puts server-wide announcements in the chat box specifically so they survive a busy screen, and BedWars stops using a quoted line the moment the message needs an answer: its party invite is the one entry on that page rendered as a captioned card, with the sender's name and a picture slot beside it. Four sources, four channels, and the split is never about how important the message feels.

rules.rule: The engine's own notification is bottom-right, at most two buttons, five seconds by default. Match that corner or knowingly take another one — and never take it by accident.
rules.why: StarterGui's SendNotification documentation fixes all three. A custom stack in a different corner is fine until anything at all calls SetCore, at which point the player has two notification systems on screen; the decision has to be made rather than defaulted into.

rules.rule: A notification that needs an answer gets AT MOST TWO ACTIONS, and if it needs three it is not a notification.
rules.why: The platform primitive caps it at two buttons, and every actionable notification found in a shipped game is binary — accept or decline a trade, accept or decline a backpack request, accept or decline a suggested item. Nothing read here has a third branch.

rules.rule: One event, several audiences, SEVERAL TEXTS. Write the message the losing side reads and the message everyone else reads as two separate strings.
rules.why: BedWars tells the team that lost its bed that they will no longer respawn, and tells every other team which colour fell. Adopt Me warns the player giving too much that scamming is bannable, and warns the other one that they may be being scammed. Two independent games, same structure: a single templated string with the subject swapped would be wrong in both.

rules.rule: Make every notification dismissible by tapping it, in addition to its timer.
rules.why: BedWars states that all of its notifications can be cleared by clicking or tapping, and the author of the banner module lists 'not clickable' as a defect of his own product. A lifetime alone leaves a player who wants the screen back with nothing to do.

rules.rule: Refusals go in the SAME channel as everything else, and the refusal names what to do instead.
rules.why: BedWars sends 'not enough diamonds', 'party is full' and 'failed to join the queue' through the identical notification stack that announces a teammate's purchase. Blox Fruits goes one step further: its immune-enemy message names the ability that fixes it and puts the key to press in brackets. A refusal that only says no is a refusal the player has to leave the game to understand.

rules.rule: Consider giving the refusal LESS chrome than the success, not more — and a different edge of the screen.
rules.why: The notification kit's Alert template is red text at the bottom with no card behind it, reserved for what could not be done. That is deliberately the opposite of the instinct to make errors louder, and it is defensible: a 'not enough money' fires constantly during normal play and does not deserve the same panel as a level-up. Recorded as a decision to weigh, because only one source read here makes it.

rules.rule: Cap the stack with a MAX-ON-SCREEN, and partition unrelated notifications into separate stack groups so a burst in one does not bury the other.
rules.why: The notification kit carries both as attributes on the template frame, and they are the only explicit answer found anywhere in this research to what happens when several fire at once. The banner module that has neither ended up exposing a public 'how many are active' call, which pushes the same problem out to every call site.

rules.rule: Anchor a stack by PLACING its template, and let direction, duration, sound and animation live on that frame as attributes.
rules.why: 'Where you move it in Studio is where its notifications appear' — and because the behaviour is attributes rather than code, duplicating the frame yields a second stack that already works. A system where position is an argument and timing is in a script cannot be restyled without being rewritten.

rules.rule: Let the CARD grow to fit the text. Never let the text shrink to fit the card — and check that no size constraint is quietly defeating AutomaticSize.
rules.why: A banner module shipped with text that shrank, its author listed the distortion as a con, the thread proposed AutomaticSize, and the author answered that the UI uses a size constraint and will not scale even with automatic sizing on. THE THREAD DOES NOT END THERE: the fix shipped in Update 2.0 as a card that resizes, and the author later says it was done WITH automatic sizing, after converting Scale to Offset and splitting the card into smaller frames. So the constraint did not defeat AutomaticSize permanently — it defeated it until the card was restructured. That is the useful shape of the trap: the symptom looks like a font problem, the cause is a constraint, and the cure is surgery on the layout rather than one property.

rules.rule: Give colour a small fixed vocabulary, decide deliberately whether a colour is carried by the CHANNEL or by the MESSAGE, and put a stroke behind coloured text.
rules.why: Blox Fruits does both on one page: three of its four tables declare a single colour for the whole section ('All of the following messages appear red in the chat boxes') while the Player Messages table colours line by line — red for danger and refusal, green for a gain, gold for an item found, magenta for materials, a blue-violet for an ability unlocking, with gold and magenta each carrying a second meaning elsewhere on the same page. So the per-message vocabulary is real but loose, and it is not how the server-wide lines are coloured at all. The stroke is that wiki's majority treatment, on 24 of its 37 coloured lines rather than on all of them; the argument for putting it behind all of yours is that coloured text over an arbitrary game world costs more legibility than it adds without one, which is reasoning rather than citation.

rules.rule: One notification may carry a gain AND its caveat, coloured differently, rather than splitting into two.
rules.why: Blox Fruits announces finding a fruit in green and, in the same message, warns in red that dying before eating it will lose it. Splitting that would let the warning be dismissed separately from the thing it is about.

rules.rule: A REWARD POPUP NAMES THE ITEM, NOT THE CONTAINER IT CAME OUT OF — and states how many things are coming before it opens.
rules.why: Tower Defense Simulator shipped a playtime claim popup that displayed the chest's name and corrected it to display the item given in v1.75.2, then added a count of how many chests a tier awards in v1.75.3. A popup that names the box has told the player nothing they were waiting to learn.

rules.rule: Announce each resource on its own line; never roll a multi-resource reward into one summary.
rules.why: Blox Fruits has separate announcements for money earned, experience earned with the weapon it was credited to, fragments earned, and materials obtained with a quantity — and no combined line anywhere in the 174 messages the page transcribes. (The money, EXP and fragment icons in those rows are the WIKI'S own templates, not something the page says the game draws; the only glyph transcribed inside a message string is the coin on the item-drop line. The per-line split is the finding; the icon is not.) The same reasoning the shop file records for itemising a bundle applies here: a count is not comparable, a list is.

rules.rule: Keep the displayed STREAK and the index into the reward calendar as two different numbers.
rules.why: Tower Defense Simulator's login rewards repeat on a 28-day table while the streak counter carries on to 29 and beyond. A day tile bound to the streak count renders nothing at all on day 29, and a streak label bound to the table position tells a 200-day player they are on day 4.

rules.rule: When a timed action can be confirmed, make the countdown BECOME the confirm control, and reset it whenever the thing being confirmed changes.
rules.why: Adopt Me's trade counter counts from 5 and turns into the green accept button, resetting every time either player adds or removes an item — and the wiki states the reason outright: it stops a player accepting after the contents changed. A timer beside a live button is a race the player can lose.

rules.rule: An unanswered actionable notification EXPIRES, and a blocked one notifies the sender instead.
rules.why: Adopt Me expires a trade request left too long, and when the recipient has requests turned off the SENDER is prompted about it. Roblox's push-notification documentation lists seven non-delivery cases, the last of which splits in two — and it also says the throttle case comes back as 'transparent feedback', so some of those failures report themselves and some do not. Delivery is never to be assumed at either end.

rules.rule: Give every notification CLASS its own off switch, and where a prompt exists only to ask permission, offer a third value that grants it standingly.
rules.why: BedWars lets friend-join notifications be turned off by themselves; the notification kit ships an individual switch per announcement trigger; Adopt Me's backpack-viewing consent is always allow, always ask, or never allow, defaulting to ask. 'Always allow' is the interesting one — it does not mute the notification, it removes the interaction that would have raised one.

rules.rule: Express a countdown to a scheduled event as discrete announcements at decreasing intervals, not as a persistent widget.
rules.why: BedWars sudden death fires at 59 seconds, at 10 seconds, and then at the event. Blox Fruits does the same for its presents event, at ten minutes, at five or one, and then at 'starting' — its other timed events pre-announce at two minutes and one. Neither game spends permanent screen space on a clock for something that happens once.

rules.rule: When a cap is reached, say WHAT WAS EVICTED to make room.
rules.why: BedWars reports that placing a new trap destroyed the oldest one and that a ninth spirit removed an older one, rather than simply refusing. Applied to the notification stack itself this is the honest reading of a max-on-screen cap: a notification silently dropped because three others were already up is an outcome the player never learns, and that is the one case where 'nothing was shown' is indistinguishable from 'nothing happened'.

rules.rule: Put the subsystem's name in brackets at the front of any message the player's own action did not cause.
rules.why: BedWars prefixes its bed-alarm and host-announcement lines that way. The prefix is what tells a player the line is not feedback on the button they just pressed, which is otherwise indistinguishable in a shared stack.

rules.rule: Compose a badge or award icon for a CIRCLE, at 512×512, before composing it for the card.
rules.why: Roblox's badge upload trims and crops to a circular icon and the documentation shows the failure case of text cropped away. A custom badge notification that reuses the uploaded icon inherits that crop whatever shape the card is.

rules.rule: On the OUT-OF-EXPERIENCE channel: the title is already the game's name, the body is 99 characters, it is a parameterised template with an asset id, and you get one per player per day.
rules.why: All four are stated in Roblox's experience-notification documentation. The one-per-day throttle is the design constraint that matters — it makes 'which single thing is worth today's slot' the actual question, and a generic come-back-and-play does not merely underperform, it spends the only slot there is.

rules.rule: Never build a notification around false scarcity, a promised free thing that is not free, or a deadline that does not exist.
rules.why: Roblox's notification guidelines ban all three by name, with a ten-minutes-or-miss-out example given as the prohibited case. This is the vocabulary a reward popup reaches for first, and on the notification channel it is a policy violation rather than a style choice.

limits: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A CAPPED STACK OVERFLOWS IS THE WEAKEST PART OF THIS FILE AND SHOULD BE FIXED BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED. One source names a 'Max on screen' attribute and a 'Stack group' attribute, and that is the entire evidence base for concurrency. Nothing read here says whether the oldest is evicted, the newest is queued until a slot frees, or the excess collapses into a '+3 more' row — and no shipped game's wiki describes its own stack overflowing at all. The rule above about naming what was evicted is an EXTENSION of a BedWars rule about trap caps to a surface that source was not talking about, and it is marked as such rather than dressed up as an observation.

NO NUMERIC COUNT BADGE WAS FOUND EXCEPT ONE. The brief asked about badge counts, and across eleven sources the only true count-in-a-corner is Adopt Me's spectator tally on the trade window. Nothing states a convention for an unread count on a HUD button — no dot-versus-number rule, no cap such as '99+', no rule for what clears it. A generator asked for a notification badge on a menu button is still working from the model's memory rather than from anything read here.

ONE HARD DURATION FIGURE EXISTS IN THIS ENTIRE FILE: the platform's five-second default for SendNotification. No source read here gives a measured toast lifetime, slide-in duration, easing curve, card width, corner radius, padding, stroke weight or font size. Nothing in this file should be used as a measurement, and the geometry has to come from the genre file the notification is being built in.

THE BLOX FRUITS COLOUR VALUES ARE THE WIKI'S TRANSCRIPTION OF WHAT EDITORS SAW IN GAME, not colours sampled from a running client. What survives scrutiny is that colour is used to separate kinds of message inside one chat channel, and that a text outline accompanies most coloured lines — 24 of 37, not all of them. The hex values are secondhand and must not be copied as tokens, and the per-colour meanings are a tendency with same-page counterexamples (gold for an item found AND for a shop restock; magenta for materials AND for a stored sword) rather than a fixed mapping.

FANDOM SERVES ITS ARTICLE HTML BEHIND CLOUDFLARE, so every wiki row was read through api.php as wikitext. That is the same content, but it means the SCREENSHOTS those pages embed were named and not seen. Every claim above is one the page states in prose or in a table; none is inferred from an image nobody looked at. Where a page's gallery captions describe a state — an already-claimed daily reward, for instance — that was deliberately NOT recorded as an observation, because a filename caption is not a description of a screen.

THREE OF THE ELEVEN SOURCES ARE KITS AND MODULES RATHER THAN SHIPPED GAMES. A kit describes what its author thinks a notification system needs, which is evidence about convention but weaker than evidence about what players actually met. The two most load-bearing structural claims in this file — the three-channel split and the stack-group/max-on-screen model — both rest on kits. They are corroborated on the channel question by two shipped games and on the stacking question by nothing.

NOTHING HERE COVERS MOBILE PLACEMENT, SAFE AREAS OR THE TOPBAR. A toast in the bottom-right on a phone competes with the jump button; a banner across the top competes with the Roblox topbar, whose 36-pixel offset the StarterGui reference mentions in a different section. No source read here addresses either collision.

NOTHING HERE COVERS LOCALISATION OR ACCESSIBILITY. The 99-character cap and platform text filtering are the only text constraints found; no source discusses what a notification does when translated text is twice as long, or how any of this reaches a player who cannot see the colour that carries the meaning. Given that the colour vocabulary rule above makes colour load-bearing, that second gap is a real one and is named here rather than left implicit.

THE DAILY-REWARD PANEL ITSELF IS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-DOCUMENTED HERE. screen-rewards.json already covers day strips, calendars, claimed/claimable/locked/missed tiles and the claim button from ten references. What this file adds on that subject is only the notification side — the popup that fires on join, the claim popup's content, the streak number that outruns the calendar, and the routing message that points at the screen. If the two files ever disagree about a day tile, screen-rewards.json is the one that looked at it.

THREE READS, AND THE ERRORS GOT SMALLER EACH TIME — WHICH IS THE ONLY THING ABOUT THIS FILE'S ACCURACY WORTH TRUSTING. Researched once and then re-read adversarially twice, all on 2026-09-20, with a repair after each. FIRST HOSTILE PASS: four claims corrected, every one the same shape — the sentence AFTER a true citation, where the page's words were extended into a statement the page does not make. It over-counted the notification kit's shipped triggers (eight listed, four shipped); it borrowed a 24-hour claim window from a wiki page's superseded history section and applied it to the current version, which states no window at all (deleted rather than hedged); it rendered the banner author's 'SizeConstraint' as 'UISizeConstraint', naming a class the source never named; and it read 'reorder up to 50 badges at once' as a cap on how many badges a game may hold. Three observations narrowed, one clause deleted, one rule made to name an effect instead of guessing a mechanism. SECOND HOSTILE PASS: eleven items, finer than the first four — five refuted outright, five plausible, one unverifiable. Five were MISCOUNTS: 'several hundred' transcribed messages where the page has 174; an outline on 'almost every' coloured line where it is 24 of 37; six documented non-delivery paths where the doc lists seven bullets covering eight outcomes; ten BedWars notification types in a sentence that then named twelve; and 'three of which are paid' where four of four are. Three were SCOPE ERRORS: colour described as per-message when three of that page's four tables declare it per section; a 28-day ladder's shape described from one of its three tracks; three login-reward tracks assigned to 'an earlier version' when the current section is itself three tracks. One was a FIRST-PAGE READ PRESENTED AS A WHOLE-THREAD READ — the DevForum JSON endpoint returns 20 posts of a 98-post thread, and post 41 held the ending of the story that row was telling. One was an inherited GLOSS: a party invite's 'avatar thumbnail' read off a placeholder image file, which is the exact move this file's own Fandom limit says not to make. Note what that pass also proves: the 'three of which are paid' clause did not survive the first repair, it was INTRODUCED by it, and the first repair's own summary repeated the wrong figure. THIS THIRD PASS re-fetched every source named in those eleven items and edited 23 places — 11 in the references, 9 in the rules, 2 in the limits, and the provenance line. Two claims were DELETED outright rather than narrowed: the party invite's avatar thumbnail, and 'with its own icon' in the per-resource-line rule. Eight more were narrowed to what the page actually says, with exact counts in place of the adjectives. The eleventh was not a claim about a game at all — it was the first repair's own assurance that it had removed no reference and invented nothing, which cannot be checked; it went out with the entry that carried it and is restated below as an open question rather than a fact. Seven of the twenty-three edits were DUPLICATE SITES found by grepping the file for each corrected claim's distinctive words — the outline overstatement had three copies (an observation, a rule's why, and a limits entry), the 'several hundred' figure two, the paid-packs miscount two including the correction record itself, the avatar gloss two, and the banner sizing trap two — the rule's why still ended at the argument when the thread it cites had since ended at a fix. One further sentence was narrowed on sight while re-reading rather than because a pass named it: a countdown rule read 'Blox Fruits pre-announces its events at ten minutes, five, one and now', which is one event's schedule, not the page's. No reference was removed in this pass; the count has been eleven throughout. WHAT IS STILL NOT SETTLED, BY NAME. (1) How a player's CURRENT Login Rewards track is chosen: the page says 'randomly chosen' and 'permanent' only about the pre-10-June-2026 version, and says nothing about the three tracks it currently lists. (2) What the BedWars party-invite image cell actually renders — the wikitext holds a placeholder image file and no image was looked at in any source for this file. (3) What a capped stack does on overflow, which is the first limit in this list and is unchanged after three passes. (4) The first pass's claim that it removed no reference and invented no observation CANNOT BE CHECKED: this file is untracked in git, so there is no prior revision in the repository to diff it against, and that claim is the editor's word rather than a verified fact. A fourth read would find something. The point of this entry is that it would be smaller than these, and that a file saying so is worth more than one claiming to be clean.
